market_context: United States; USDA composition for firm tofu and cooked chicken breast
title: Tofu vs Chicken: A Nutrition Comparison

seo.title: Tofu vs Chicken: Protein, Calories, Fat and Nutrients
seo.meta_description: Chicken breast has much more protein per 100 g; tofu adds fiber, unsaturated fat and can provide substantial calcium depending on the coagulant.
seo.search_intent: Compare firm tofu and chicken breast using realistic amounts and explain why they are not nutritionally identical substitutes.

excerpt: Cooked chicken breast is much more protein-dense, at about 31 grams per 100 grams versus roughly 15–18 grams in firm tofu. Tofu contains more fat, some fiber and can be a major calcium source when made with calcium sulfate. Both can anchor a protein-rich meal, but they are not gram-for-gram equivalents.
content_html:
Tofu and chicken can occupy the same place in a meal, but nutritionally they are not a one-for-one swap. Chicken breast concentrates far more protein; tofu contributes fiber, plant fat and minerals that depend heavily on how the tofu was made.

If the goal is maximum protein for relatively few calories, chicken has the advantage. If you want a plant protein that also contributes unsaturated fat and some fiber, tofu does a different job.

A per-100-gram comparison

Firm tofuCooked chicken breast
Calories~130–150~165
Protein~15–18 g~31 g
Fat~8–9 g~3.6 g
Fiber~1–2 g0 g

The protein gap is large: chicken can provide almost twice as much at the same weight. The calorie gap is much smaller because tofu contains more fat.

A normal serving of either can still provide substantial protein

About 5 ounces of firm tofu provide roughly 21–25 grams of protein. Five ounces of chicken breast provide around 44 grams.

If a plant-based meal is aiming for 30 grams of protein, tofu may need support from edamame, beans, grains, seeds or another source. The same chicken serving already exceeds that target.

Tofu fat comes mainly from soybeans

Tofu contains more total fat, but much of it is unsaturated. Skinless chicken breast is much leaner.

This helps explain why tofu and chicken can be relatively close in calories despite a huge difference in protein per 100 grams.

Tofu calcium can vary several-fold between products

When tofu is set with calcium sulfate, a serving can provide several hundred milligrams of calcium. Tofu made with another coagulant may contain far less.

The label is therefore the best way to judge calcium; it is not a fixed property of every block of tofu.

Chicken provides B12 naturally; tofu does not

Chicken contributes vitamin B12, niacin, vitamin B6 and selenium. Tofu provides nonheme iron, some magnesium, fiber and soy compounds, but it is not a reliable natural source of B12 unless fortified.

Soy protein is high quality

The lower amount of protein does not mean tofu has an ‘incomplete’ protein. Soy supplies all nine essential amino acids in favorable proportions and has good digestibility.

The practical distinction is simply that there are fewer grams of protein in 100 grams of tofu than in 100 grams of chicken breast.

Cooking method can overwhelm the base-food comparison

Breaded fried tofu can absorb substantial oil; breaded fried chicken can too. The comparison above stops applying when one food is cooked with large amounts of added fat and the other is not.

The useful rule

Chicken and tofu can both anchor a meal, but they have different profiles. Chicken is far more protein-dense; tofu combines plant protein with unsaturated fat, some fiber and, depending on the product, substantial calcium. Choose based on the whole diet rather than expecting exact gram-for-gram equivalence.

faq.question: Which has more protein, tofu or chicken?
faq.answer: Cooked chicken breast has about 31 g/100 g versus roughly 15–18 g/100 g in firm tofu.

faq.question: Is tofu a complete protein?
faq.answer: Yes. Soy provides all nine essential amino acids in favorable proportions.

faq.question: Does tofu contain calcium?
faq.answer: It can contain a lot when set with calcium sulfate; other tofus contain much less, so check the label.
